Path: studio — a translated label survives an edit | 缺项 (Studio's nav-item inspector shows a locale-map label as `[object Object]`, and one keystroke writes a plain string over the whole map, so every other locale's text is lost) | P2

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:studio` · `pm:queue`. Direction: objectui#11128's rule on the second editor, through the **same** helper, so the canvas and the inspector cannot disagree

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (`StudioNavItemInspector`) ⇒ `domain:ui`. It is the sibling objectui#11128's contract review asked for.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-09-29T23:01Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why p2.** It takes objectui#11128's grade (p2): the same loss of authored translations, on the second editor of the same label.
- It is not p1 because the input shows `[object Object]` before any keystroke. So the author is told the label is not what was authored.
- It is not lower because after PR objectui#11146 the canvas beside it keeps the map, while this inspector still deletes it.

**Direction.**
- **Display.** The inspector resolves the label through the spec's `resolveI18nLabel(label, locale)`, in the designer locale, the way the canvas does.
- **Edit.** An edit writes only the designer locale's entry of a map and keeps every other entry. A plain-string label stays a string.
  - It uses PR objectui#11146's `renamedLabel` (`previews/AppNavCanvas.tsx:198`, module-private today), moved to one module both editors import.
  - ⛔ No second copy of the key choice (exact tag, else bare language, else a new exact-tag entry).
- **Keys.** `title` / `name` are not read as a nav item's label.
- **Pins:**
  - a map label shows the resolved text under en and under zh;
  - an edit under zh changes only `zh-CN`;
  - a plain string edits as it does today;
  - PR objectui#11146's canvas pins stay green.

**Serial.** `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is also PR objectui#11152's file (objectui#11136, ACCEPTed and open) and objectui#11153's. They are different components in one file: whichever lands second rebases. The dispatching seat reads PR objectui#11152's state at claim.

  - display: `curLabel` (`:1464`) resolves through `resolveI18nLabel(label, locale)` in the designer locale;
  - edit: `patch({ label: e.target.value })` (`:1476`) writes only the designer locale's entry of a map and keeps every other entry. A plain string stays a string;

Why no: a Studio editor keeps what the author wrote, and a module-private helper moves to a shared internal module. No schema, prop, type or accepted set moves.
